title: PLDT Home champions safer digital spaces for Filipino families, calls for shared responsibility in protecting children online
summary: As Filipino children increasingly turn to the internet for learning, entertainment, gaming, and social interaction, PLDT Home underscores the importance of helping parents create safer digital…

blocks.text: As Filipino children increasingly turn to the internet for learning, entertainment, gaming, and social interaction, PLDT Home underscores the importance of helping parents create safer digital environments where children can explore, connect, and grow responsibly.

blocks.caption: Protecting children online. PLDT Home led the Safe Online Spaces Forum, inviting various sectors to share their insights on keeping children safe online and the safeguards that need to be implemented. Present during one of the panels were (L-R) Butch Jimenez, PLDT Chief Operating Officer and Chie…

blocks.text: PLDT & Smart reinforced this message during the Safe Online Space Forum, held on September 29, 2026, at Makati Shangri-La Hotel. The Forum brought together representatives from government, law enforcement, telecommunications companies, digital platforms, schools, child-protection organizations, mental-health experts, parents, and other stakeholders to discuss practical ways to strengthen online protection for Filipino children.

Convened amid growing concerns about children’s exposure to harmful online content, interactions, and communities, the Forum emphasized that keeping children safe online requires more than technology alone. It calls for greater awareness, open communication, and coordinated action among families, schools, industry players, and government institutions.

blocks.caption: Butch Jimenez, PLDT Chief Operating Officer and Chief Technology Officer, calls for a multi-sector approach to protect children from online threats.

blocks.text: Butch Jimenez, PLDT Chief Operating Officer and Chief Technology Officer, emphasized that protecting children online requires collective action, with every sector playing a role in developing meaningful solutions.

“This problem is not solved by just telcos playing God or even the DICT. It’s solved when every sector in this room works together to understand the problem and come up with a solution. We are not bystanders in this. We are people who can help,” Jimenez said.

His message set the tone for the Forum’s discussions, which highlighted how stronger collaboration among industry players, government institutions, schools, and families can help address online risks and create safer digital environments for children.
Building a safer digital home starts with parents
For many Filipino families, the home is where children first discover the digital world. As access grows, parents must better understand the platforms their children navigate daily.

Rather than relying solely on restrictions or monitoring, parents are encouraged to take an active role: familiarizing themselves with popular platforms, engaging in regular conversations about online experiences, and creating an environment where children feel comfortable raising concerns.

blocks.caption: Joy and Edric Mendoza, parents of six kids and co-founders of Homeschool Global, talk about encouraging open dialogue with their kids to build relationships with them at home.

blocks.text: “As parents, we want to set rules for our kids. But how is our relationship with our kids? We have to ask ourselves if we know what our kids really enjoy. When we learn to enjoy their interests with them, their hearts turn towards us, their parents,” said Edric Mendoza, Chairman and co-founder of Homeschool Global. “We believe that if we have a strong relationship, that’s when we can implement rules and protocols.”

“What the online space does is to introduce competing subcultures that go against your values as a family. When our kids are younger, we want to teach them values, to have convictions and discernment to know right from wrong,” added Joy Mendoza, co-founder of Homeschool Global. She also highlighted the importance of constant conversations with kids to strengthen their bonds.

Beyond the home, schools also play a crucial role in shaping children’s digital habits and helping them navigate online risks. As children increasingly bring their online experiences into classrooms and peer interactions, closer collaboration between parents and educators becomes essential to creating safer, more supportive environments for young people.

blocks.caption: Teacher Tin Canon speaks on the role of schools and educators in protecting children from online threats.

blocks.text: Teacher Tin Canon, who specializes in family life and child development, shared that although the education sector is overwhelmed, many teachers like her are ready to guide children in school and support their parents. “If a child verbalizes that they will harm somebody or themselves, schools have to treat it as an emergency situation. Schools have to pivot. We also connect with parents to have that trusting relationship with their kids, not just solely expect educators to have all the solutions.”
Helping families recognize and respond to online risks

Practical digital safety involves teaching children simple, defensive habits: avoiding harmful content, reporting suspicious interactions, safeguarding personal information, and confiding in trusted adults when they feel unsafe.

Online Alerto, PLDT Home’s digital safety advocacy, supports these efforts by raising awareness of online risks and equipping Filipino families with practical information to navigate the digital world more safely.
Through digital safety education and stakeholder partnerships, Online Alerto continues to reinforce the importance of responsible internet use and parents’ role in protecting children online.
Online safety is a shared responsibility

While parents are the first line of defense, they cannot manage complex digital risks in isolation. Telecommunications providers, digital platforms, schools, government agencies, and advocates must work together to improve preventive measures, reporting channels, and support systems.

Building on the call for collective action raised during the Forum, discussions explored opportunities for closer cross-sector collaboration, including clearer reporting and escalation processes, stronger digital literacy efforts, and practical interventions to help protect children.

For PLDT Home, these conversations reinforce its commitment to helping Filipino households enjoy the benefits of connectivity while promoting greater awareness of the responsibilities that come with it.

As digital technology continues to shape how Filipino families live, learn, and communicate, PLDT Home remains committed to promoting safer and more responsible online experiences through education, advocacy, and collaboration.

Because building a truly connected home goes beyond providing access to the internet. It also means helping families gain the knowledge, confidence, and support they need to navigate the digital world safely.
